Sample type: Postmortem serum (left ventricle, autopsy 23 h after death), 3-month-old digitalised infant
Study method details: Forensic case investigation of a 3-month-old digitalised infant who died 2 h after the third dose, plus method comparison across four RIA methods and HPLC fractionation. Postmortem serum (autopsy 23 h after death) diluted 35-fold with the NML 0 standard; analyses in duplicate; Sep-Pak C-18 extraction and RP-18 HPLC with 30-s fraction collection and RIA of every fraction; carryover blank gradient run; recovery verified by RIA and 3H-digoxin. RIA Method 2 (sequential) has 50% of the DLIS cross-reactivity of RIA Method 1 with identical digoxin cross-reactivity, so a fall of Method 2 relative to Method 1 is the study's DLIS test.
Additional sources of bias: n = 1 postmortem case; 35-fold dilution into the assay 0 standard could itself alter matrix and is not discussed; the highest DLIS magnitudes quoted (10 microgram/L serum, 20 microgram/L bile, 80 microgram/g meconium) are from other or unpublished work, not measured here; "The relative importance of DLIS interference in cases of suspected digoxin toxicity is unknown."
Notes: Table 1, replicate 1. NEGATIVE result for DLIS: the sequential method (which halves DLIS cross-reactivity) did not fall relative to the standard method. Table 1 bottom line "Average overall: 71.5"; Discussion p 656: "In the present case, the serum contained 71.5 +/- 3.6 microgram/L digoxin immunoreactivity." Therapeutic range printed p 650: 0.8-2.0 microgram/L. Values below the analyser detection limit were assigned zero ("none detected"). Separately, 180 plasma samples from patients treated with digoxin were assayed in duplicate for method comparison.
